claims.text: CeO2 nanorods used as supports have exposed, readily reducible (110) facets.
Strong interfacial bonding forms between the HEA nanoparticles and the reducible CeO2 support.
Nanoparticle–support interfacial bonding significantly constrains atomic mobility at the interface.
Constrained interfacial mobility maintains structural and chemical homogeneity from 473 to 1923 K.
Free-standing HEA nanoparticles have greater atomic diffusion than CeO2-supported nanoparticles under identical conditions.
Greater atomic diffusion in free-standing nanoparticles causes phase segregation and compositional inhomogeneity.
CoNiCuZnPd HEA clusters can be formed on CeO2 nanorods.
The initial CoNiCuZnPd nanoparticles are a homogeneous, single-phase solid solution.
Support-induced anchoring limits both surface and bulk atomic mobility.
Limiting atomic mobility suppresses thermally activated diffusion and phase separation.
Supported CoNiCuZnPd HEA nanoparticles will retain uniform oxidation states, coordination environments, and composition throughout 473–1923 K thermal and redox cycling.
Free-standing CoNiCuZnPd nanoparticles will develop measurable compositional changes and phase-separated regions during the same cycling.
CeO2-supported HEA nanoparticles will have greater catalytic activity than otherwise identical free-standing HEA nanoparticles.
CeO2-supported HEA nanoparticles will have better thermoelectric properties than otherwise identical free-standing HEA nanoparticles.
Alternating reducing and oxidizing atmospheres over 473–1923 K mimic both catalytic and thermoelectric operating environments.
Intrinsic ordering could stabilize the nanoparticles independently of the support interaction.
In situ XAS can monitor oxidation states and local coordination changes during redox cycling.

contradictions.description: The predicted-outcome field calls the free-standing sample the baseline, whereas the baseline field defines the baseline as the homogeneous initial state before high-temperature treatment. These are different comparators.
